summary:
Adana Province has no provision of its own on gender identity, documentation, policing or facilities, and the source record carries no local enforcement data for the province. A trans visitor to Adana is therefore dealing with the Turkish national framework, set at national level and applied here without a provincial overlay.

The statutory baseline is permissive on its face. Same-sex sexual activity has been legal since 1858 under the Ottoman penal code, and transgender people have been able to change their legal gender since 1988, the year gender reassignment surgery became lawful. Türkiye has no comprehensive law prohibiting discrimination on the basis of sexual orientation or gender identity, and LGBTQ people are barred from serving openly in the military.

Same-sex relationships receive no legal recognition. Marriage, civil unions and domestic partnerships are unavailable, and same-sex couples cannot adopt jointly or as individuals. A trans visitor in a relationship read locally as same-sex should expect no recognition of that relationship in Adana.

A leaked draft omnibus justice reform, the 11th Judicial Package, would enable criminal charges against LGBT people countrywide if adopted. Human Rights Watch described it on 29 October 2025 as one of the most alarming rollbacks of rights in decades; Istanbul activists held a press conference against it on 28 October 2025. The package contains no province-specific provisions and would apply in Adana as everywhere else in Türkiye. Whether it has since passed is unresolved in the sources.
tangentialFactors:
The draft 11th Judicial Package is a national measure with no Adana-specific content, but its adoption would change the legal exposure of any LGBT person in the province, including visitors. Human Rights Watch's characterisation of it as one of the most alarming rollbacks of rights in decades indicates the direction of national policy rather than a local Adana development.

Adana Province appears in the source record only as a jurisdiction without its own provisions; no local incident data, policing statistics or facility practice for the province was identified, so the national assessment carries the risk picture here.
localsOnly:
Residents of Adana Province live under the same national baseline as visitors: legal gender change has been available since 1988, same-sex sexual activity has been legal since 1858, and no comprehensive discrimination protection exists on grounds of sexual orientation or gender identity. Open service in the military is barred for LGBTQ personnel.

Same-sex couples in Adana cannot marry, enter a civil union or domestic partnership, or adopt jointly or individually. The province maintains no separate provisions on any of these matters.

Local LGBTI+ residents are exposed to the same draft 11th Judicial Package as the rest of the country, which would permit criminal charges under vague provisions if enacted. No Adana-specific enforcement record, detention data or reported incidents were available in the sources.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether the 11th Judicial Package has been adopted since Human Rights Watch reported on it on 29 October 2025 is unresolved in the sources.

No Adana-specific finding was available in the source inventory; the province-specific layer of this record rests on the absence of local provisions rather than on documented local practice. Local enforcement data, detention figures and incident reports for Adana were not sourced and remain unverified.
